findings.claim: Without signature verification the webhook endpoint trusts any POST body, letting an attacker activate holds without paying.
The check-then-insert in POST /api/holds is a race: simultaneous requests for one unit both see zero active holds. A unique partial index or serializable transaction is required.
findings.evidence: const existing = await sql`select id from holds where unit_id = ${unitId} and status = 'active'`;

findings.claim: The plan assumes checkout.session.completed carries an expanded payment_intent with charges inline, but Stripe sends only the PaymentIntent id string and charges are not included, so pi.charges.data[0] throws.
findings.evidence: session.payment_intent gives us the PaymentIntent with its charges inline

findings.claim: An hourly expiry cron means a 72-hour hold can stay active up to 59 minutes past expires_at, which brokers will notice.
